chunks: Many faces will be contrite on that day,

key_terms.وُجُوهٌ: Faces (often used metonymically for the people themselves)
key_terms.يَوْمَئِذٍ: On that day (referring to the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for faces to be 'contrite' or 'humble' on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Ghashiyah is often contrasted with the 'shining' faces of the righteous, emphasizing that true humility (khushu') stems from deep self-awareness of divine majesty rather than mere ritual. The Ahl al-Bayt tradition highlights this state as the ultimate result of purifying the soul through obedience to the Imams, distinguishing it from the superficial awe of the general populace. This spiritual posture reflects the believer's recognition of their own insufficiency before the Perfect Judge.
